Was I a morally bankrupt asshole? Yes, yes I was. Would we have a standing Army without morally bankrupt assholes like me? Probably not, and then we'd have to have a draft every time our country went to war.

This story is about my favorite recruit. I know his name by heart, it was one of those guys with two first names like Ricky Bobby.

To tell this story, I have to give a little history on Ricky. He lived in a small town that had two parts, the extremely rich, who owned lakefront property, and the extremely poor, who lived in trailers and houses hidden away by the woods. In high school Ricky was dating the sheriff's daughter, and he was the one she was going to marry, yadda yadda yadda. The sheriff didn't like that because Ricky was from the poor part of town, but he was going to let it slide because his daughter was in love. Long story short, Ricky was quite the heartbreaker, wasn't very faithful, and she found out and left him. The Sheriff decided he wasn't going to let that slide anymore.... Ricky done broke the wrong daughter's heart.

After that, Ricky was under arrest for almost everything. He had to drop out of high school because he missed too many days being in jail and all that. Ricky was under arrest one night for yelling at his sister in front of the deputies when they showed up, not even any physical altercation.

I meet Ricky about two years after this. I was a fresh new recruiter, doing everything I was supposed to, going around town, talking to folks. I meet Ricky, and he tells me that he probably can't join the Army because of his law violations. I tell him that he doesn't know that yet, meet me at the recruiting station, and we'll see what we can do.

I had only been on recruiting duty a month, and I figured that I knew everything from my six weeks recruiter course.

Ricky didn't even have a GED at the time, so this was like a trial run. I ran his police records and everything, and holy fucking cow, his rap sheet was like 2-3 pages long. I could not make sense of it. But, his convictions were only 6... All misdemeanors, and one over the limit.... Something really didn't add up though, the charges that he did have convictions on, he had less arrests for. I really could not make sense of it. I put Ricky's packet away, but I just knew I was missing something.

You see, when you get a case like that, where you're just stuck, you pass it off, let a fresh set of eyes look at it, and that's what I did. Every recruiter in the recruiting station had hands on Ricky's packet at one time or another, and everyone said that he was toast, but I didn't give up. I just knew something was wrong. He had around 2 dozen arrests, but only six convictions, but he was convicted of one charge that he had never even been arrested for.

A year passes, I still have Ricky's packet in my desk. By this time, I'm a seasoned recruiter. Time to go back through Ricky's packet. I reestablish contact with Ricky, and let him know not to get his hopes up, but I'm still working his packet.

At this time, I'm more confident, have contacts in the local courts, and threw away all ethics.

I talk to the court about it and tell them to fix their error. The problem was that he yelled at his sister and mother, so they arrested him for one change, then charged him twice, but one case hadn't been closed out. So they closed it out...... with time served, putting him one conviction over the limit for the Army....

I said, fuck that, they can't charge you twice for the same crime, that's bullshit. Oh, and in that one year break, Ricky racked up another arrest and lost his job because of it. He had like two dozen arrests, but only six actual charges, and that last charge they charged him twice.

My plan, send him down to MEPS on Mission Day(quota day for the month) and hopefully they'll be too swamped to make sense of his paperwork that took me over a year to make sense of.

....

They caught it.

Now, on mission day, the 1SG is down there at MEPS making sure everything goes right. This was a hiccup. He personally called my station commander to let him know what's up.

Back at the station, "Yo, Peen, your boy didn't make it through."

"Oh well. I guess I'll just have to tell him sorry. I told him not to get his hopes up." I had already put 3 people in that month, so I was above my quota.

"No, Top says 'Make it happen', you need to fix this."

Whoa!

How the fuck am I going to make charges disappear, after 6 pm, and with no possible way? How?

At this point in time, after a year on recruiting duty, I was a renowned document forger. 1SG's "Make it happen" just meant to me that he was aware.

Now here's the thing, the military runs your fingerprints through the FBI database, which shows everything you've been arrested of, and the disposition of those cases. Ricky had never been arrested for the last charge he was convicted of, so it wouldn't show up in the FBI database, right?

Well, I was about to find out. I grabbed another packet of someone who I had put in the Army, and had a dismissed charge. I scanned Ricky's conviction sheet, scanned the dismissal sheet, and transferred the relevant parts over. I've done much better work, but this had to be done immediately, so it was sloppy as fuck. All I could hope for was that the faxed copy wouldn't show, and that my guess about the FBI database was right.

Who fucking knows what laws I broke that night. I basically forged a judge's signature onto a form he didn't sign. I was definitely in violation of UCMJ.

I was sweating bullets after that. Dude, I could go to jail for that shit. I shredded the "original" document, the forgery before the fax.

About 45 minutes pass, "He's in."

Only my station commander and I knew that I did that. 1SG was more about he didn't care as long as he didn't know. I mean, he fucking knew, but how could you prove it?

I got the "Recruiter of the Quarter" award for that one. Oh, Ricky counted as a Grad Alpha because he scored higher than a 50 on the ASVAB, and passed this personality test.

Ricky joined the Army, and as far as I'm aware, he was successful while he was in.

The last time I spoke with him, he was home on leave, hooking up with some lady with 3 kids, and a husband who was out on the oil rigs, and she wanted to leave her husband to be with him.... I was like, "Ricky, after all the trouble you've been through, do you really think this is a good idea?"

I know nothing of his story after that.

The point of the story was about the lengths I would go to put people in the Army, even after I had met my quota. I'm sure there have been at least a thousand others like me that sacrificed their integrity to meet the demands of the Army. We were at war in two different countries, at a time both wars were unpopular.

One thing I never did though, was lie to the recruits to get them to sign up. That was like my mental justification for breaking my integrity.

"I will lie for them, but never to them."

And I even broke that moral code when I told that one recruit that he did pass his GED before he shipped out. That was the only time though.
